### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/scripts/vlm/a03_two_phase_commit_driver_v1.mjs#L29 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Require unique render evidence pages** For multi-page observations, this only checks each render evidence row against the `page_chain` map; two rows can both name page 1 while page 2 is absent, as long as the array length still matches. `prepareCommit` then accepts an observation whose render commitment omits one of the pages it is supposed to cover, so a tampered or malformed checkpoint can pass the conservation gate with incomplete visual evidence. --- https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/scripts/vlm/a03_two_phase_commit_driver_v1.mjs#L73 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Bind receipt fields to the ledger event** When validating persisted committed receipts, the top-level sequence/previous hash used by the chain check is not compared with `ledger_event.sequence`/`ledger_event.previous_event_hash`, and the embedded event fields are not rebound to the request. A committed checkpoint can therefore pass validation with top-level `previous_event_hash` set to the admitted head while the hashed `ledger_event` actually points at a different predecessor, so standalone checkpoint validation can accept a broken ledger chain. --- https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/scripts/vlm/cie9709_ledger_broker_v1.py#L114 **![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat) Preserve broker response compatibility** The host probe in `scripts/vlm/probe_cie9709_host_v1.py` still rejects any response whose key set differs from the old six fields via `set(response) != expected_response_keys`, so adding fields here makes every successful broker append fail with `broker_response_failed` before event readback. This breaks the parent/host validation path for non-A03 callers that use the broker. --- https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/scripts/vlm/a03_two_phase_commit_driver_v1.mjs#L76 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Require all candidates before COMMITTED** When a persisted checkpoint is marked `COMMITTED` but contains only a subset of receipts, `validatePreparedCheckpoint` still returns true because it validates only the entries present in `committed` and never compares that count with `candidates.length` for the terminal phase. Any consumer that trusts this exported validator/readback can accept a partial 175-object wave as fully committed. --- https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/scripts/vlm/append_only_access_ledger_v1.py#L243 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Reject duplicated operation IDs during verification** With idempotent retry semantics, `operation_id` becomes a uniqueness key, but `_parse_and_verify()` still accepts a valid hash chain containing the same `operation_id` twice; this scan only notices it on a later append of that same ID. That lets `verify()`/readback report a ledger as valid even though duplicate operations have already been admitted, which contradicts the duplicate-operation fail-closed path. --- https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/scripts/vlm/a03_two_phase_commit_driver_v1.mjs#L64 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Enforce unique objects when validating checkpoints** `prepareCommit()` rejects duplicate `source_identity.object_key`, but `validatePreparedCheckpoint()` does not repeat that check when loading/resuming a checkpoint; it only accumulates operation IDs. A checkpoint with two different payloads for the same object and a recomputed collection hash passes validation and can be committed, omitting another expected object while still meeting the expected count. --- https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/scripts/vlm/a03_blind_checker_inspection_v1.mjs#L206 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Check every skipped page in a chain gap** For a jump such as `[1, 4]`, this checks only page 2 (`previous + 1`) and accepts if any continuation ref contains `"2"`, leaving page 3 unaccounted for; substring matching also lets ref `12` satisfy missing page 2. Such a page chain omits source pages while passing inspection, so observations and render commitments can be built over an incomplete question span. --- https://github.com/Samsen879/ciecopilot-home/blob/eb6ef1a8f803cc0447f9057aa8275bdd8b0c6c49/artifacts/method-map/v1-9709/pdf-first-rebuild/gold/e1-source-adjudication-v1/checker/checker-observations.v1.json#L19623 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Use a schema that admits the A03 artifacts** These A03 artifacts declare the frozen A01 schema version, but `campaign-a-a01-evidence.v1.schema.json` has no `checker_observations` artifact type and its `durable_readback`/`validation_bundle` definitions require different fields/verdicts; schema validation rejects the new files. Any downstream gate that validates the declared schema will fail before it can consume this evidence.
